svg.title: Why more time to exhale works, and what it costs
svg.desc: Idealized passive linear model with illustrative numbers; inspiratory time held at 1 second and tidal volume held constant. Two sections: 20 breaths per minute, a 3 second cycle with 2 seconds to exhale, and 10 breaths per minute, a 6 second cycle with 5 seconds to exhale. In each section a volume panel plots a fast unit with a 0.5 second time constant, solid, and a slow unit with a 2.5 second time constant, dashed, as percent of the received volume remaining against expiratory time. At 2 seconds, where the next breath begins, the fast unit has 2% left and the slow unit 45% left, that is 98% and 55% emptied. At 5 seconds the fast unit has about 0% left and the slow unit 14% left, about 86% emptied; a tick on the slow curve at 2.5 seconds marks one time constant, 63% emptied. Beneath each, a flow panel on the same time axis, in arbitrary units, shows expiratory flow decaying; at 20 per minute the slow unit's flow is still present when the next breath starts, and at 10 per minute it is near zero. A box gives each unit's resistance and compliance, notes that the fast unit's initial flow is 5 times the slow unit's for the same volume, and warns that real lungs have many units, flow limitation and stiffer tissue at high volume, so a trace that returns to zero does not prove every region emptied. A bottom strip gives the slow unit's trapped volume per 100 mL delivered, about 82 mL at 2 seconds and about 16 mL at 5 seconds, and the cost: minute ventilation falls from 10 to 5 L/min at a tidal volume of 0.5 L, so PaCO2 rises, and whether that is tolerable depends on pH, oxygenation, brain and heart.

g.text: LIFE-THREATENING ASTHMA
Why more time to exhale works,
and what it costs
Passive linear single-compartment units.
Inspiratory time 1 s and tidal volume held
constant. Illustrative numbers, not patient data.

Units and limits
Fast unit τ 0.5 s (R 10 × C 0.05): solid. Slow
unit τ 2.5 s (R 50 × C 0.05): dashed. R in cm
H2O·s/L, C in L/cm H2O. Fast unit’s initial
flow is 5 times the slow unit’s for the same
volume.
Real lungs: many units, flow limitation,
stiffer at high volume. A trace that returns
to zero does not prove every region emptied.
What it buys, and what it costs
Slow unit trapped volume per 100 mL delivered:
≈82 mL at 2 s, ≈16 mL at 5 s.
Cost: minute ventilation 10 → 5 L/min (VT 0.5
L). PaCO2 rises; whether it is tolerable
depends on pH, oxygenation, brain and heart.
